Ostrow Mazowiecka Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ostrów Mazowiecka, Poland

Demolished. Jewish settlement in Ostrów Mazowiecka is confirmed from the 18th century; the town's rabbis included Jehoszua (from 1843) and later figures connected to prominent Hasidic families, Gerszon Henoch Leiner and Bencijon Rabinowicz. By 1921, 6,812 Jews made up half the town's population. In September 1939, Germans killed about 300 Jews; on November 11 that year, between 300 and 800 more were shot, and the remaining Jewish population was forced out entirely. A postwar Jewish Committee registered just 23 members in 1947. This cemetery, probably established by the 1780s based on a parish visitation record, was later paved over for a Communist-era market with stalls and a cooperative building; today it lies entirely beneath a shopping center, car repair shop, and marketplace.
